subject: Medford Teachers Association Contract Negotiations
overview: The Medford School Committee received updates on adaptive physical education, playground safety inspections, and the district's labor relations posture amidst FY23 budget planning. Representatives and members of the Medford Teachers Association and allied unions attended in force to protest proposed wage increases and working conditions during ongoing collective bargaining negotiations.

items.title: Consent Agenda and Donations
items.summary: Approved meeting minutes, bills, payroll, and two severed donations totaling $2,000 for McGlynn Middle School.

items.title: Subcommittee Reports
items.summary: Approved meeting minutes from the Communication and Family Engagement Subcommittee concerning student absenteeism letters and the district communication platform, as well as the Rules and Policy Subcommittee regarding attorney and dress code policies.

items.title: Superintendent's Updates
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent highlighted recent community grants from Tufts University, school clean-up efforts, and student achievements including a regional championship win for the high school robotics team.

items.title: Report on Unified Sports and Adaptive Physical Education
items.summary: Staff reported on the successful implementation of the district's adaptive physical education program servicing roughly 40 students and expanding unified sports offerings.

items.title: Medford School Choice Status
items.summary: Voted to maintain Medford's status as a no-school-choice district for the upcoming academic year.

items.title: McGlynn Playground Inspection Report
items.summary: Heard a report detailing safety inspection results, routine childhood injury statistics, and design plans to replace the aging McGlynn playground with a universally accessible structure.

items.title: Labor Relations and Operating Budget Update
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent David Murphy presented an overview of negotiations with the district's 10 collective bargaining units and outlined $2.4 to $2.6 million in projected fixed cost increases for the FY23 budget.

items.title: Public Participation on Ongoing Contract Negotiations
items.summary: Medford Teachers Association President Charlene Douglas, union leaders, and educators voiced frustration over proposed 2% wage increases, loss of elementary prep time, and educator burnout during contract talks. A motion introduced by Member Ruseau to make bargaining ground rules public was withdrawn following legal cautions from the administration.

items.title: New Business: Correction to Policy BEDH
items.summary: Suspended rules requiring two readings and approved numbering corrections to Section 3 of Policy BEDH regarding public comment and presentations.

items.title: Reports Requested and Condolences
items.summary: Clarified procedural handling for outstanding report requests, read condolences for former educators and community members, and observed a moment of silence.
